# Chapter 11: The Present

Coffee with Cindy was the morning ritual that grounded everything else. They took it in the kitchen, in the condo that overlooked the water, watching the sun rise over Lake Michigan through windows that faced east. The coffee was simple—drip, no sugar, cream for Cindy—and the conversation was simple too, the kind of talk that didn't require subjects or conclusions, that simply existed because two people were awake at the same time in the same room.

Bob was seventy-two
